subject: Reserved capacity: sizing options, term flexibility & GPU price-index trigger
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cobaltlabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity: sizing options, term flexibility & GPU price-index trigger

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our notes, Cobalt's Q4 launch will need a steady 24/7 inference footprint for the first 12 months and a potential 2x burst for a 4–6 week onboarding window. I put together two sizing options and a short set of term structures for you to review (attached).

Quick ask: can you confirm whether you prefer a fixed-sku reserved commitment (e.g., 40 V100-equivalent slots) or a flexible pool with an execution window that lets you shift between medium/high-memory SKUs if usage shapes change? Cobalt mentioned sensitivity to sudden GPU market price increases — you asked about a protective clause tied to a GPU price index.

What we'll do on our side:
- Provide a baseline discounted rate for a 12‑month commit and a larger step discount for a 24‑month commit.
- Offer an optional mid-term "swap window" (one-time, 30-day) to reallocate reserved SKUs within the agreed pool.
- Propose a GPU price-index trigger that can convert price changes >X% into credits or a temporary rebate rather than reopening the discount schedule.

Next steps: if you can confirm preferred sizing option by Friday, we'll draft a term sheet and show the modeled unit economics with both the swap window and the index-trigger behavior.

Best,
Jasmine
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Cobalt_capacity_plan_v2.xlsx, pricing_sensitivity_model.csv
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cobaltlabs.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobaltlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: sizing options, term flexibility & GPU price-index trigger

Thanks Jasmine — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) We prefer the flexible pool approach if the economics are similar. Our workload might skew to more memory-bound SKUs after pilot, so the ability to swap would be valuable.
2) For the GPU price-index trigger, we would expect protection if cloud GPU spot/market prices increase by more than ~12–15% relative to an agreed baseline. Ideally that becomes an automatic credit to offset our invoice rather than requiring a contract amendment.
3) From a commercial perspective, Samir and I need to understand the credit budgeting/limit and whether that reduces the initial discount offered.

Can you circulate a straw term that shows: (A) a 12-month vs 24-month price table with and without swap window, (B) an example showing a 15% GPU index spike and the resulting credit calculation? If you can include a DocuSign preview for procurement to start reviewing, that accelerates us.

—Alex
VP Engineering, Cobalt Labs
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cobaltlabs.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: sizing options, term flexibility & GPU price-index trigger

Alex — looping in Neha and Marcus to confirm the commercial model and the approval path. Draft terms attached (draft_mop_terms.docx) along with the sensitivity model. Below I've pasted the key tradeoffs so everyone is aligned.

On the swap window: we can support a one-time 30‑day SKU reallocation inside the committed pool. That requires a short notice window (7 days) and we model expected delta consumption to assess any top-up billing.

On the GPU price-index trigger: two structurally different approaches we can run by procurement:
A) Credit-based safety net: if our agreed GPU index rises >15% vs baseline, Cobalt receives a one-time credit equal to X% of monthly committed spend (cap applies). This preserves the original discount tiers but budgets the protection.
B) Discount re‑pricing (approval required): index breach would trigger a re-pricing conversation and potential downward price adjustment for future invoices (requires finance + sales leader approval).

Internal ask (Neha / Marcus / Aditya): can you confirm what cap we should propose for the credit-based approach (percent of monthly committed spend and absolute cap), and whether we can offer the swap window without an additional premium for the 24-month commit?

Jasmine
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: sizing options, term flexibility & GPU price-index trigger

Thanks for the context. Quick recommendations from finance/portfolio planning: 

1) Cap for credit-based safety net: propose credit = 50% of committed monthly spend for a single month, capped at 3x monthly committed spend over the life of the contract. Rationale: this hedges short shocks but prevents unlimited exposure.

2) Threshold: 15% index increase is a reasonable trigger. For anything between 8–15% we can offer a graduated one-time partial credit (25% of monthly committed spend) to avoid frequent escalations.

3) Swap window economics: for a 24‑month commit we can include a single 30‑day swap window at no additional premium; for 12‑month commits, include swap window but charge a small reconfiguration fee equal to 5% of monthly committed spend (covers scheduling and rebalancing ops).

4) Approval path: credits up to 1.5x monthly committed spend can be approved by Sales VP (Jasmine / Marcus). Anything above that requires CRO finance sign-off. If Cobalt asks for discount re-pricing on breach, escalate to Sarah (Head of Sales Ops) and CFO for a formal amendment — this will add ~7–10 business days.

5) Suggested commercial language snippet for the credit approach (for draft_mop_terms.docx):
"If the Redwood GPU Price Index (defined in Appendix A) increases by more than 15% relative to the baseline calculation, Redwood will issue a one-time billing credit to the Customer equal to 50% of the monthly committed spend for the following invoice. Credits are subject to an aggregate cap equal to three times the monthly committed spend over the term of the Agreement."

6) Operational note: attach the pricing_sensitivity_model.csv showing modeled P&L for Cobalt at +0%, +10%, +15%, +25% index scenarios. This is helpful for procurement to see the impact on unit cost vs list price.

I'll sign off on including the swap window for 24-months at no premium. If we get pushback on the cap, we can move to the graduated credit approach (8–15% partial credit).

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Reserved Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: pricing_sensitivity_model.csv
